summary: I could not refute any runtime claim in the record. Live reads match its numbers. Weight sizes match the HF API (Q4_K_M 19.13 GiB, NVFP4 21.82 GiB, AutoRound 20.02 GiB, UD-IQ4_XS 16.51 GiB, UD-Q2_K_XL 11.45 GiB). From config.json, KV is 20,480 B per token at BF16: 10 full-attention layers x 2 KV heads x head_dim 256. The Q4_K expert share works out to exactly 16.875 GiB. vLLM v0.33.0 registers the architecture and both parsers (qwen3_coder, qwen3) and has the offload and language-model-only flags. The 16 GB blockers are real and open: #66264, #49476 (this exact NVFP4 model OOMs on a 16 GB sm_120 card) and #66423. So the "vLLM does not fit" verdict holds. On the llama.cpp side, release v1.0.0 has the qwen35moe architecture and routes this chat template to the Qwen3-Coder tool-call parser. The server-cuda13 image tag exists. The plan recomputes to 14.0-14.5 GiB of VRAM against about 14.8 GiB usable, so 131k context with --n-cpu-moe 20 is feasible but tight. The weak point is the compute buffer, which nobody has measured: be ready to use --n-cpu-moe 21-22, or let --fit choose. Tool calls work, but open issue #30118 means some calls are occasionally missed. The speed figures are only bandwidth arithmetic. Gaps: no measured throughput or VRAM on this laptop. Ollama's offload behaviour for this model was not checked.
